name: Facial Onset Sensory and Motor Neuronopathy
aliases: Facial onset sensory and motor neuronopathy syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed diagnostic criteria for FOSMN syndrome

criteria.description: Initial onset of sensory symptoms localized to the face
Progressive involvement of motor neurons leading to weakness and atrophy
Evidence of sensory neuronopathy on clinical and electrophysiological testing
Exclusion of other causes such as ALS or multifocal motor neuropathy
EMG showing widespread denervation and sensory nerve conduction abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of facial onset sensory symptoms with progressive motor neuronopathy and sensory neuronopathy confirmed by clinical and electrophysiological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by electrophysiology; genetic testing may be performed to exclude mimics.

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or mild protein elevation
Normal routine blood tests excluding metabolic causes
imaging: MRI brain may show mild brainstem atrophy
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; genetic testing used to exclude ALS and other motor neuron diseases
other: Electromyography showing widespread denervation and reinnervation
Sensory nerve conduction studies showing reduced or absent sensory potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of prominent sensory symptoms in early stages
Typical upper and lower motor neuron signs without sensory neuronopathy
Predominantly motor involvement without sensory neuronopathy
Presence of conduction block on nerve conduction studies
Paroxysmal facial pain without progressive sensory loss or motor weakness

redFlags: Rapid progression of bulbar symptoms with respiratory compromise
Development of widespread limb weakness and atrophy
New onset seizures or autonomic instability
references: Vucic S, et al. Facial onset sensory and motor neuronopathy syndrome: clinical and electrophysiological features. Brain. 2006.
Swinnen B, et al. Facial onset sensory and motor neuronopathy syndrome: a review. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2019.
Orphanet: Facial onset sensory and motor neuronopathy syndrome (ORPHA:85162)
